revisions: 2026-09-28: receipt_sha256 names docs/profile-extraction-v3-receipt.json. The five ORDER_DETAIL rows are qualified at the tested choice level; component usage rows record what the pinned HL7apy archive can and cannot supply; a 2.8.2 component usage row records that conditional usage is not represented.

2026-09-28: database_receipt_sha256 names docs/profile-extraction-v4-receipt.json and conditions_sha256 docs/profile-conditions.json. Component usage, base field usage, length and terminology rows now describe the v5 packs built from the pinned HL7 v2 database export and the reviewed conditions; counts are over the elements promised structures reach.

rows.source_survey: The HL7 v2 database export records NA for this edition's components except a few it records O (CCD, CCP, AUI and table-specific CE variants), and the edition's chapters print no component usage; the pinned HL7apy archive declares every component (0, 1). There is no usage distinction to adopt.
rows.missing: No edition source defines component usage. v5 marks each NA component unclassified and evaluation reports each occurrence as unsupported, never optional.
rows.authoritative_source_needed: None exists for this edition; a site profile may declare component usage locally.
rows.implementation_test_needed: Covered: an unclassified component cannot pass (TestUnclassifiedUsageAndUnavailableLengthCannotPass, TestPinnedDatabasePacks).
rows.release_claim_affected: No base component usage claim for this edition.

rows.source_survey: Usage codes from the pinned HL7 v2 database export (B written as O by NIST's stated decision), with the edition table where the export carries none; each C predicate encoded from its own edition sentence in docs/profile-conditions.json with located, hashed basis spans.
rows.missing: Predicates are a reviewed reading of edition prose, since no machine-readable HL7 source states them. A C field whose edition states no condition or contradicts itself is unsupported; a condition that depends on information the message does not carry is undecided. Neither passes.
rows.authoritative_source_needed: Independent review of the encoded conditions against the edition text; exact-content rights review (#627).
rows.implementation_test_needed: Owned fixtures cover true/false/unknown predicates, parent context and prohibition (internal/profileeval/usage_test.go); broaden independently qualified message fixtures per promised structure.
rows.release_claim_affected: Field usage is evaluated from the edition's code; a conditional field passes only when its predicate is decided from the message. No full conformance claim until independently qualified and #627 is approved.

rows.missing: Zero records unavailable extracted length information; it does not establish that the standard permits unlimited length.

rows.evidence: nHapi's generated ORM_O01_ORDER_DETAIL constructor uses the three-argument add, which AbstractGroup.Add inserts with choiceElement false; no generated group of this version declares a choice element. That is an upstream model limitation, not an extraction omission. The same pinned HL7apy archive's hl7apy/v2_3_1/groups.py (lines 315 and 334) declares those six segments as one choice group, in nHapi's order, with identical remaining members.
rows.implementation: readmit-profile-extractor/v3 replaces the flattened members with one choice node in readmit-profile-pack/v4 and refuses any disagreement; evaluator v3 matches exactly one alternative per repetition. Earlier pack versions refuse a choice node.
rows.tests: TestPinnedOrderDetailChoice/2.3.1: each of the six alternatives alone passes; two alternatives in one detail and notes without an alternative fail. TestAChoiceGroupAcceptsExactlyOneDeclaredAlternative covers the operator without upstream content.
rows.remaining: Field, component and terminology constraints inside each alternative segment remain governed by the other rows of this version.
rows.release_claim_affected: Order-detail alternatives are qualified at the tested choice level only; this is not full ORM structural validation.
